name: Project Moon Life
tagline: A browser life simulator: you are born into a randomized life, pick a career track, make choices, and get an ending.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Mechanically this is a state machine with dice: a random starting seed, a stat block, a weighted event deck, a few career branches, and ending conditions chosen from thresholds. An agent can stand up a playable single-player version in one sitting with no backend, no accounts, and no sync, because nothing here needs other players or server state. The optional AI chapter feature is one API call against your own key, which is cheaper for you than any pass and also slower and less consistent. What you cannot one-shot is the part that makes it fun: hundreds of hand-written events that land, balance tuning so runs do not all feel identical, and endings that pay off. Your clone will be functional within hours and thin within three playthroughs.
coreLoopDIY: Generates a random starting life, advances year by year through weighted branching events across four career paths, tracks stats, and resolves an ending.
requirements: Optional: an OpenAI or Anthropic API key in .env if you want AI-written chapters
Willingness to write your own event text, which is most of the work
whatYouLose: The authored event corpus: hundreds of written outcomes you would have to replace yourself
Balance tuning, so your runs will feel either too random or too samey
Any visual and audio polish, pacing, and the feeling that an ending was earned
Hosted AI chapters without you paying per token and handling failures
Whatever shared or community layer exists around endings and runs
moatNotes: The engine is a weekend exercise in any language. The writing is the product, and writing does not come out of a code generator in a usable state.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because nobody plays a life sim for the random number generator, they play it for the moment a written event makes them laugh or wince. Paying for a chapter pass is paying for someone else to have already written that, plus not having to care about token bills, prompt tuning, or why your generated chapter just contradicted the last twelve years of your character's life. A self-built clone scratches the engineering itch and then sits unplayed.
notes: The simulation is trivial, the content is not; expect a working toy in an afternoon and a boring one by evening.
prompt:
Build a single-player browser life simulation game called "Lunar Lives". Empty folder, no backend database, no accounts, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable: Vite + React + TypeScript, plain CSS modules, Zustand for game state. One optional tiny Node/Express endpoint for AI chapter text, nothing else server side.

Game rules to implement:
- On "New Life", roll a random starting seed: birth year, family wealth tier, home region, and four stats (health, smarts, charm, grit) from 0 to 100.
- The run advances one year per click. Each year draws 1 to 3 events from a weighted event deck filtered by current age bracket, career path, and stat thresholds.
- Each event shows a short narrative paragraph and 2 to 4 choices. Choices apply stat deltas, money deltas, and can set flags that unlock later events.
- At age 18 the player picks one of four career paths: science, trade, arts, drift. Each path has its own event pool and its own milestone events at fixed ages.
- Ending conditions: health hits 0, age exceeds 85, or a path specific terminal event fires. Resolve one of at least six endings from final stats, money, and flags, and show a run summary timeline of every choice made.
- Deterministic seeded RNG (seedrandom or hand rolled mulberry32) so a seed string replays identically. Show the seed and let the player paste one in.

Content: put all events in src/content/events.json with a typed schema (id, minAge, maxAge, paths, requires, weight, text, choices). Ship at least 60 events across the brackets as placeholder content and document the schema in README so more can be added without touching code.

Persistence: localStorage only. Autosave the current run, keep a history of the last 20 completed runs with seed, ending, and final stats.

Optional AI chapter: a POST /api/chapter endpoint in server/index.ts that takes the run timeline and returns one prose chapter. Key from .env (MODEL_API_KEY), never in client code. If the key is missing, hide the button, do not crash.

Out of scope: multiplayer, leaderboards, art assets, sound, mobile apps, payments.

Deliver: npm install, npm run dev serves the game, npm run server runs the optional endpoint. README explains the event schema and how to add a new career path.
